text:
The tone of the email is authoritarian, abrupt, and dismissive. It uses commanding language ("It's been decided without room for negotiation," "Make the necessary arrangements") which can come across as disrespectful and demotivating to employees. A more professional and respectful tone would acknowledge the inconvenience and explain the necessity of the request, fostering better morale.

Suggested changes to match a more collaborative and respectful sentiment:

Subject: Request for Overtime Availability This Weekend

Hi [Name],

I hope you're having a good week.

Due to [brief reason, e.g., an urgent project deadline], we need to hold overtime hours this weekend. I understand this is an inconvenience, and I appreciate your flexibility in making the necessary arrangements to be available.

Please let me know if you have any questions or if there are any constraints I should be aware of.

Thank you for your hard work and dedication.

Best regards,

[Your Name]
